US-10052665.summary: The patent claims a cleaning device configured to selectively dispense a fluid to a surface being cleaned. The device includes a housing where the outer portion is "configured to be grasped and manipulated by a user during a cleaning procedure" [9f5af1b5d8ca]. It comprises "a dispenser comprising a porous or fluid permeable material" [9f5af1b5d8ca] and "a wiper removably attached to the wiper portion of the outer housing portion" [9f5af1b5d8ca]. The wiper is repositionable "to enable a different portion of the outer fabric layer to comprise the wiping surface" [9f5af1b5d8ca]. No motor, battery, or power source is claimed.

US-8800092.summary: The patent claims a hand-operated flat mop apparatus featuring a trigger mechanism to release a disposable cloth without manual contact. The device comprises a top plate, a push plate with spikes or hooks, a mechanical plate, linkages, ratchet collars, and compression springs. Activating the trigger allows spring force to move the push plate, releasing the cloth.

It comprises "a base layer being fashioned for receiving a user's hand" and "a storage layer, the storage layer comprising an inner side attached to the exterior side of the base layer and an exterior side opposite the inner side, the storage layer being absorbent and able to retain and subsequently dispense fluid" [31153aaae958]. Embodiments may include "a sleeve of the glove with a length extending substantially beyond the wrist of a user" [31153aaae958]. Materials specified include configurations where "the synthetic rubber is nitrile" [31153aaae958].

US-10052665.rationale: The patent covers a manual cleaning device configured to dispense fluid and wipe surfaces, aligning directly with the intended product category of non-powered household cleaning tools [9f5af1b5d8ca]. The claims describe a housing grasped by a user and a wiper removably attached to the outer housing portion, which matches the design constraints for manual mops or scrubbers [9f5af1b5d8ca]. The inclusion of a dispenser with porous material suggests a specific mechanism for fluid delivery that is commercially desirable in modern cleaning tools [9f5af1b5d8ca]. Engineering effort is moderate as the device requires no motor, battery, or power source, but does involve mechanical design for fluid dispensing and repositionable wiper attachment [9f5af1b5d8ca]. Regarding maintenance fees, the owner's decision to stop payments usually indicates the patent was worth little to them. This does apply to a new entrant in terms of reduced legal risk, as the technology is likely in the public domain. However, the low value to the original owner may not apply to a new entrant who can integrate these features into a broader product line where fluid dispensing and reversible wipers are standard consumer expectations, providing value through product completeness rather than exclusive monopoly rights.

US-10052751.rationale: The patent discloses a height adjustment lock system specifically for cleaning devices comprising a pole and cleaning head [8dd7d8547c94]. This aligns directly with the intended product category of manual cleaning tools like mops. The mechanism involves a braking cylinder and locking handle with a brake shoe pusher [8dd7d8547c94], offering a specific mechanical solution for pole adjustment common in this category. As the patent is expired due to nonpayment, the technology is in the public domain, removing licensing barriers for a small manufacturer. The original owner's decision to stop paying fees suggests the specific implementation may not have provided sufficient competitive advantage or margin to justify the cost at their scale. However, for a new entrant, the zero licensing cost allows integration of a potentially superior locking mechanism without IP risk, differentiating the product from basic fixed-height or simpler friction-lock competitors. The engineering effort is moderate as it requires manufacturing specific mechanical components like brake shoes and cylinders rather than simple snap-fits, but fits within non-powered manufacturing capabilities.

prose.executive_summary: The run looked at 2404 US utility patents in the cleaning-tool CPC groups. 299 of them appear in Official Gazette expiration notices from the last 104 weeks, 209 passed the non-powered screen and 8 were analysed. Recommended for technical and legal review: US 8,800,092 (Apparatus to remove a disposable cloth from a hand operated flat mop through a single trigger mechanism without having to touch the disposable cloth), US 10,052,665 (Devices and methods for dispensing fluids and wiping surfaces). Every status is dated and comes from public notices; none of this is legal clearance.
prose.methodology: The search began with a CPC code query. This returned 2404 candidates. The Gazette was checked for expired patents and reinstatements. This found 299 candidates that expired in the relevant window. A non-powered screen was run on all candidates. This left 209 candidates. The status of these candidates was verified. This left 210 candidates. The candidates were ranked. The top 8 candidates were analysed. 201 candidates were not analysed. 2 candidates were recommended.
prose.commercial:
All candidates align with the intended product category of non-powered household cleaning tools. US 8,800,092 and US 10,052,665 receive Shortlist recommendations while the others receive Hold recommendations. US 8,800,092 describes a trigger mechanism for releasing disposable cloths. The assembly involves ratchet collars and compression springs. This requires higher precision than static mop heads. US 10,052,665 covers a manual cleaning device configured to dispense fluid. The inclusion of a dispenser with porous material matches design constraints for manual mops. Engineering effort for both is moderate as neither requires a motor or battery.

The Hold candidates involve different mechanical systems. US 10,052,751 discloses a height adjustment lock system involving a braking cylinder. US 8,826,487 claims a mop cleaning set with a dehydration device. Both require mechanical design and tooling for plastic components. US 8,826,487 carries a flag for a related active continuation. US 10,065,611 claims a windshield cleaning implement with an arcuate shaft. The specific automotive application limits direct relevance to a general household cleaning product line compared to the floor cleaning focus of the other candidates. All five patents list expired status due to nonpayment.
prose.next_steps: For US 8,800,092, verify the mechanical complexity of the trigger mechanism. Assess manufacturing feasibility and costs. For US 10,052,665, evaluate the fluid dispensing mechanism. Confirm compatibility with intended cleaning solutions. Check wiper attachment mechanisms for durability and ease of use.
